targets.title: Asset Pricing with Liquidity Risk
targets.evidence_quote: We begin by replicating the LCAPM tests of AP using their original methodology, which is based on GMM and uses portfolios as test assets. We cover their original time period of 1962 to 1999 and a more recent period 2000 to 2015.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: As will be obvious momentarily, our replicated tables do not obtain the identical numbers as the original tables. Thus, we have not been able to “quantitatively replicate” AP results in the sense that Ivo Welch describes in his editorial in this issue.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: In summary, our extension results always fail to support that the main Lee two-beta LCAPM predictions hold at the same time.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original-period market observations are reanalysed from CRSP/Compustat; comparable numerical output exists but substantial second-stage discrepancies remain. Alternative model specifications and liquidity measures also test the original 1962–1999 period and undermine the liquidity-risk finding. Later-period and NASDAQ samples alone are not treated as robustness evidence.

reasoning: The paper combines reproduction of the original 1962–1999 observations with new-period replications and extensions; reproduction is selected for its explicit original-number comparison. Acharya and Pedersen is the single target paper. Lee supplies the alternative estimator and model parametrization, and is compared as related evidence; the paper does not frame its analysis as a retest of Lee’s separate finding. No original DOI is printed in the reference list.
